summary.name: QuietSpeech
summary.one_liner: A native macOS menu bar app that dictates, edits, and generates text in any Mac app using Apple's on-device speech recognizer and Apple Intelligence, activated with a one-time $29 license.
use_cases: dictating messages in Slack or Mail
rewriting a selected paragraph by voice
drafting text from a spoken request
adding @mentions by voice in chat apps
summary.what_it_does: QuietSpeech lets you hold the Fn key, speak, and have cleaned-up text inserted at your cursor in any Mac app. Dictation uses Apple's on-device speech recognizer, with filler removal and punctuation handled by Apple Intelligence; if Apple Intelligence is off, rules-based cleanup is used instead. It has three modes: dictate, edit a selected passage by voice, and generate a new draft from a spoken request. A custom vocabulary can be set for names and jargon, and saying "at Priya" in chat apps produces a real @mention. It skips AI polish in code and terminal apps.
notable: Uses Apple's on-device speech and Foundation Models frameworks, so no API key is needed
One $29 license covers two Macs with no account, and includes a 14-day refund
Native app using under 60 MB of memory in the menu bar
Optional connection to OpenAI, Groq, Ollama, or a custom endpoint
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later and an Apple silicon Mac (M1 or newer)
Edit and generate need Apple Intelligence on, or a connected provider; if a provider is connected, that provider receives the data
License check needs internet once every 14 days
